newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Strong day in generally weak market.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Strong day in generally weak market.

text.p: Six companies made their market debut on Wednesday after initial public offerings and all garnered solid premiums despite some recent malaise in the new issues market.

The largest IPO, Swisher International Group Inc SWR.N, raised $102 million in a six million share offering at $17 each. Shares of the Jacksonville, Florida cigar maker edged up 1/8 to 17-1/8. Merrill Lynch was the lead underwriter of the IPO.
Swisher's IPO had rated generally high marks by IPO analysts due to its niche in the popular cigar industry.
"We had some weakness in the beginning of the month but this week has been pretty decent for IPOs," said Vince Slavin, who tracks initial public offerings for Cantor Fitzgerald.
Some of the strength may have come from the elimination of deals which did not spark stellar demand. Many IPOs have been postponed or moved to early 1997.

Another deal which had been forecast to do well was Procom Technology Inc by Montgomery Securities. The stock rose over ten percent, up 1 to 10 from its IPO price of $9 a share. The company makes data storage and access systems.

The Millbrook Press Inc was the highest rising IPO of the day with shares jumping almost 30 percent, up 1-1/4 to 5-3/4 on their first day of trading for the Brookfield, Connecticut children's book publisher.
Other companies that made their IPO debuts today:
-- Software company Credit Management Solutions Inc rose 1-5/8 to 13-1/8.
-- Accent Color Sciences Inc, which makes high-speed color printing system, rose 3/4 to 8-3/4. Cowen was the lead underwriter of the offering.
-- Lithia Motors Inc offered 2.5 million shares of Class A common stock for $11 each, below its estimated pricing range of $13 to $15. The Medford, Oregon company operates car dealerships.
-- Intellicell Corp shares rose sharply, up 1-3/8 or about 27 percent to 6-3/8. The company distributes wireless communications products.
